title: Sharp Non-Commuting Operator Constants, Quantitative One-Shot Converse Sharpenings, and Constructive Lean 4.35.0 Formalization for Universal Quantum Randomness Extraction
abstract: Regula and Cheng (arXiv:2611.33270v1) establish tight one-shot bounds and optimal asymptotic error and strong-converse exponents for quantum privacy amplification under universal hash families by introducing half-quadratic (err_hq) and fully-quadratic (err_sq) binary quantum hypothesis-testing errors. We sharpen their quantitative one-shot theory in three directions and provide a complete machine-checked constructive formalization (UNIV-EXTRACT-CERT-1.0). First (Theorem A), we prove that err_sq(A||B) <= err_hq(A||B) <= (25/16) err_sq(A||B) holds for all (possibly non-commuting) positive semidefinite operators A, B >= 0 on any Hilbert space via the explicit spectral-clipping POVM phi(M_0) = min(I, (5/4) M_0) and the Loewner perfect-square identity (25/16)(I - M_0)^2 - (I - (5/4) M_0) = (1/16)(5 M_0 - 3I)^2 >= 0, proving exact equality iff A and B commute and A = (3/2) B on supp(A) intersect supp(B) when err_sq(A||B) > 0, and completing the exact sharp constant triangle (25/16, 4/3, 2). Second (Theorem B), we exploit the sign flip 1 - 6p(1-p) <= 0 for |Z| in {2,3,4} and exact truncation norm A(p) = (1-2p)^2 + (1-p)/2 to sharpen their 4*-universal one-shot leftover-hash converse constant from 1/3 to C_sharp(p) = (1-p)/(2 max(A(p), sqrt(B(p)))) > 1/3 for every finite |Z| = 1/p >= 2, featuring an exact rational regime transition at p* = 1/8 (A(1/8) = B(1/8) = 1) and peaking at C_sharp(1/4) = C_sharp(1/5) = 1/2 (+50% over 1/3). Third (Theorem C), we retain the dropped |Z|-1 factor in Lemma 19 and repair a factor-of-2 scaling typo on p. 40, strengthening the 2-universal prefactor from 1/4 to |Z|/(4(|Z|-1)) (doubling to 1/2 at |Z| = 2). All 22 Lean 4.35.0 theorems compile with zero sorry, zero custom axioms, and zero Classical.choice, paired with an AST-audited zero-float verifier, 16 JSON certificates (including explicit GF(q) degree-3 4*-universal hash families), and 59 unit and forgery-rejection tests.
